column2: Both dimensions are doing real work — loosening either the start-range cap or the bill-range floor monotonically increases both cohort count and observation count.

The two dimensions have roughly comparable bite. Moving the start cap from $2k to $4k at any fixed bill floor adds 30–60% more cohorts. Moving the bill floor from $10k to $7k at any fixed start cap adds 70–110% more cohorts. So the bill floor is somewhat more sensitive but they are in the same ballpark.

The strictest cell ($2k start / $10k bill) yields 144 cohorts and 469 observations (~16% of rows). The loosest cell ($4k start / $7k bill) yields 400 cohorts and 1199 observations (~42% of rows). About 2.8x more cohorts and 2.6x more observations between the corners.
Marginal effect of the start cap is roughly constant in absolute terms across bill floors. At $7k bill
